boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Bristoe Station record (October 14, 1863) in the Bristoe Campaign [October-November 1863]. The morning fight at Auburn is the separate frozen record VA041. Campaign-wide marches, captures, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Corps; the live field reads zero. Humphreys gives the Second Corps 8,243 enlisted infantry present for duty on the October 10 return, but says Warren had about 3,000 infantry and three batteries on the field, two brigades being with the train; he gives Hill's corps 17,223 enlisted infantry, including Cooke's brigade, and Ewell's about 15,000 on the September 30 return. Hill says Heth's three brigades advanced.
claims.rationale: Returns and engaged figures differ in date and scope; none is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Hill says he saw the Federal Third Corps resting and hurried to attack, and that Cooke came upon the Second Corps behind the embankment, of whose presence he was unaware. Humphreys says Hill's guns opened on the rear of the Fifth Corps, that Warren had been warned the enemy would probably send a column to Bristoe, and that Lee was as ignorant of the Union dispositions as Meade was of his.
claims.rationale: Hill names the Third Corps and Humphreys the Fifth; the identification is disputed. Attributed knowledge from interested accounts.

claims.value: Hill says he is convinced he attacked too hastily. Lee's indorsement says Hill overlooked the Second Corps in his haste, which caused the disaster; Seddon calls it gallant but over-hasty; Davis cites a want of vigilance. NPS says Lee angrily told Hill to bury his dead and say no more. Humphreys calls the Second Corps' handling admirable. The frozen and live commanders are Lieutenant General A. P. Hill and Major General G. K. Warren.
claims.rationale: Judgments are attributed; the NPS remark is not in the inspected reports. The frozen commanders do not receive automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 1,980 total; the live field reads 1,920 (US 540; CS 1,380). Humphreys gives the Second Corps' loss at Auburn and Bristoe as 30 officers and 403 men killed and wounded and the Confederate loss in both actions as 782 killed and wounded, citing the Medical and Surgical History, besides 450 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Humphreys' totals combine Auburn and Bristoe and are not assigned to this record.

open_questions: Warren's, Webb's, Hays's, Heth's and Cooke's reports and the Third Corps casualty return (not printed with Hill's report) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Humphreys is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff in 1863–64, per his publisher's list. Stuart's, A. P. Hill's and Lee's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIX, Part 1, are separate families of interested Confederate commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
